answer: Agents resist Sybil attacks by requiring every identity to post forfeitable collateral, so a thousand sock puppets cost a thousand times as much while honest agents pay once. Duplicates that misbehave get their stake slashed, leaving attackers stranded on a barren tundra of locked value. Trust is built only through repeated verified exchanges, letting reputation forge and spread like a vine, climbing over genuine history instead of sprouting instantly for free. The economics invert the attacker's advantage: fake identities burn resources, while real agents compound their bond into credibility.
